title: KV cache metric loss retrospective and runbook proposals
body:
SUMMARY:
During a model variant rollout on 2025-10-29 we observed a rapid drop in kv_cache_hit_ratio metrics across several dedicated pools which coincided with an SLO burn alert for 95th-percentile response latency. The immediate pager noise was dominated by repeated SLO-burn alerts and downstream high-latency errors; initial oncall mitigation reduced customer impact but underlying metric loss persisted for ~3 hours in some pools.

Why this doc exists:
- capture timeline, observations, and hypotheses that were missed in the first-pass incident notes
- propose short-term runbook additions and medium-term observability changes to prevent recurrence and reduce pager noise
- record experiments run during mitigation and the outcomes

INCIDENT TIMELINE (condensed):
- 2025-10-29 02:12 UTC: Canary rollout of model variant v2.7 begins (traffic split 10%).
- 2025-10-29 02:18 UTC: Ops-oncall receives first SLO-burn alert for model-route /generate (95p latency > 1.5s for 10m window).
- 02:20–02:35 UTC: Alerts escalate; dashboards show kv_cache_hit_ratio dropping from ~0.88 to ~0.05 in pool-gamma.
- 02:25 UTC: Eviction metrics spike (kv_cache_evictions/sec) on nodes with memory pressure after jit-load of new weights; some exporters timed out.
- 02:30 UTC: Synthetic heartbeat metric kvcache_heartbeat_missing fires; some exporter instances missing.
- 02:45 UTC: Temporary rollback of v2.7 on canary; rate-limited traffic routing to fallback model variant. SLO alerts reduce but metric gaps remain intermittently.
- 05:10 UTC: All nodes show recovered kv_cache_hit_ratio; post-incident monitoring remained for 72h.

KEY OBSERVATIONS:
- The observable metric that tripped alerts (SLO burn) was downstream of an internal signal (kv_cache_hit_ratio). The cache hit drop amplified token-level latency, increasing the tail.
- Some telemetry streams (kv_cache_hit_ratio, kv_cache_evictions) were partially missing because the exporter process on a subset of GPU nodes had crashed/restarted during eviction storms, causing metric holes that confused rate-based alerts.
- Alerts were firing from two sources: (1) direct SLO burn on latency; (2) derivative alarms on kv_cache_hit_ratio (sudden drop). The combination created duplicated pages.
- Existing alert definitions do not differentiate between sustained low hit ratio and short exporter reporting gaps. This caused the oncall to chase symptomatic signals.
- There was no concise triage runbook step that told oncall to check exporter health vs actual application latency path (i.e., is the metric missing vs real drop).

ROOT-CAUSE HYPOTHESIS (multi-factor):
1) v2.7 increased memory allocation pattern and promotion behavior in the serving runtime which caused bulk KV cache evictions on warm nodes.
2) Eviction spike temporarily overloaded the exporter and the node’s telemetry agent, causing incomplete metric emission for ~1–4 minutes on affected hosts.
3) Alerting rules treated both telemetry outages and real cache degradations equivalently; derivative thresholds were too tight and lacked a grace/smoothing window.

EXPERIMENTS & MITIGATION STEPS EXECUTED DURING INCIDENT:
- Immediate rollback of canary rollout (02:45 UTC) to reduce pressure. Outcome: latency improved within two minutes for most requests.
- Throttled cache rebuild using a serve-side backoff (hotfix in runtime) to avoid mass eviction storms (temporary config). Outcome: reduced eviction/sec peak by ~65% in trial pool.
- Restarted exporter process on 3 affected nodes; restarted instances restored metric emission. Outcome: missing metric time-series patched, but retrospective showed gaps in historical series.
- Temporarily muted derivative kv_cache alerts while SLO alerts were active to limit duplicate paging. Outcome: reduced human churn but risked missing an ongoing cache problem.

MONITORING GAPS IDENTIFIED:
- No exporter-heartbeat-based suppression: we lacked a reliable synthetic exporter heartbeat that would gate lower-confidence metric alerts when exporter is flaky.
- Alerts use absolute threshold on kv_cache_hit_ratio with 1m aggregation; this is noisy during transient exporter restarts.
- No explicit pairing between exporter health metrics and derived SLO/metric alerts (i.e., alert annotations to indicate exporter state).
- Dashboards did not show a quick view comparing metric emission rate (samples/sec) vs service traffic; hard to determine metric loss vs real drop quickly.

RUNBOOK PROPOSALS (short-term additions):
1) Triage checklist (first 6 actions for any SLO-burn that mentions KV cache or similar internal metric):
   - A. Check 95p latency panel and request traces for increased decode/hot-path ops. (owner: oncall)
   - B. Check exporter_heartbeat and exporter_uptime on all nodes; if heartbeat missing > 20s, treat metric as low-confidence. (owner: oncall)
   - C. Check kv_cache_evictions/sec and memory-pressure events on nodes; if evictions spike + exporter heartbeat gaps, escalate to infra oncall. (owner: oncall -> infra)
   - D. If exporter missing, avoid immediate kv_cache_hit_ratio-derived paging; instead create a temporary incident annotation and watch for real latency SLOs. (owner: oncall)
   - E. If both exporter and real latency are elevated, follow rollback/traffic-shift play (product/infra). (owner: release-engineering)
2) Add explicit runbook step: when metric gaps present, prioritize real-user-impact signals (SLO/trace error rate) over missing internal telemetry.
3) Muting rules: replace manual muting with a small state machine that triggers automatic mute of derivative alerts when exporter_heartbeat == missing for >15s, with auto-unmute after 5m once heartbeat returns.

ALERT TUNING PROPOSALS (mid-term):
- Replace 1m single-window kv_cache_hit_ratio alerts with a dual-window rule: short window (1m) for detection but require corroboration with either exporter sample rate or sustained drop in 5m window to page.
- Add a low-confidence tag to alerts fired when exporter sample rate < 60% of expected; route these to a lower-severity channel (ops-internal) not the primary pager.
- SLO alerts: add context to SLO alert payload identifying whether internal cache metrics are healthy, so responder can triage faster.

OBSERVABILITY ENGINEERING TASKS (medium-term):
- Implement exporter heartbeat metric (kvcache_exporter_heartbeat) emitted every 10s; baseline expectations per node.
- Dashboard: create a single-pane “metric-fidelity” row showing samples/sec, last-emitted timestamp, exporter restarts, and overlap with traffic volume for the route.
- Create synthetic twin test: a low-cost synthetic request that validates cache path and records kv_cache_hit_ratio from controlled input every 5m; use this synthetic to surface cache logic regressions prior to rollouts.
- Add automated pre-rollout gating: run the synthetic twin against candidate model variants in a staging pool for 15 minutes; fail rollout if synthetic shows >30% drop in hit_ratio or >2x eviction rate vs baseline.

COMMUNICATION / POST-INCIDENT NOTES:
- Customers with Dedicated pools in region us-west-2 saw the most impact; coordinated cs notifications were sent during mitigation.
- Internal postmortem owners: eng-serving-runtime for code change; eng-observability for alert/runbook changes; release-eng for rollout gating.

ACTION ITEMS (owner + target date):
- Implement kvcache_exporter_heartbeat metric and basic dashboard (owner: Morgan Chen) — target 2025-11-20.
- Change kv_cache alert rules to dual-window + low-confidence tagging (owner: Priya Raman) — target 2025-11-17.
- Add runbook triage checklist to oncall playbook and train oncall rotation (owner: Aisha Patel) — training session 2025-11-25.
- Add synthetic twin for cache path and integrate into rollout gate (owner: Tom Alvarez) — prototype by 2025-12-05.
- Postmortem writeup for exec (short exec summary) (owner: Evan Brooks) — draft 2025-11-14.

OPEN QUESTIONS / DISCUSSION POINTS:
- Should we move to exporter-side buffering to avoid metric loss during high eviction storms, or is restart-and-reconnect acceptable? Pros/cons are around memory/CPU overhead vs fidelity.
- What tolerance do product teams accept for rollback gating on synthetic twin failures? Must balance time-to-ship vs safety.
- Is muting derivative alerts acceptable long term, or should we rework alert routing to different oncall rotations?

NOTES ON UNRESOLVED TECHNICAL DETAILS:
- Precise memory allocation pattern change in v2.7 still under code review; PR 342 touches allocator heuristics. Need confirmation whether allocator policy or weight loading pattern is the primary trigger.
- Exporter crash logs show OOM in two nodes but not all; need deeper node-level forensic (core dumps retained).

ATTACHMENTS & QUICK LINKS:
- Datadog dashboard: kvcache health (linked_artifacts above)
- GH PR: serving-runtime PR #342 (linked_artifacts above)
- JIRA ticket for gating and heartbeat work: JIRA-OPS-1284

CONCLUDING NOTE:
This felt like a classic case of "telemetry failure amplifies symptom chasing." Primary emphasis for next cycle: make telemetry self-aware (heartbeat + low-confidence tags), add quick triage guidance to oncall playbook to reduce churn, and prevent eviction storms via release gating and runtime safeguards.

-- Aisha P. (eng-observability)
